## Result

I developed a concrete parallel fabrication process, generated ten manufacturable route layouts, ran optical and process calculations, and built a cost model that includes the two couplers, packaging, inspection and rejected devices.

**The candidate is worth a small experiment, but it does not currently meet your full invention criterion.** In particular:

- The calculations support investigating a short, multimode optical connection; they do not establish a packaged insertion loss below 3 dB.
- No manufacturing yield has been measured.
- The cost model gives approximately **$4.13 per working device**, conditional on achieving 90% yield. Comparable replication is approximately **$3.73**, and parallel two-photon printing approximately **$4.04**.
- The potentially useful distinction—selecting different nonplanar routes on identical three-dimensional stock using only a new two-dimensional mask—still needs a physical demonstration and a more extensive novelty search.

I would therefore **reject a tenfold-cost-reduction claim for this design**. I also cannot honestly replace it with a claim of a demonstrated capability that incumbents lack.

PHYSICAL DESIGN CONTRACTS FOR PARALLEL OPTICAL FABRICATION AND NET HEAT CONVERSION
ROOT,12November2026Brisbane. Engineering calculations and scoped primary inputs. No physical experiment or device performance is asserted.

1. Optical attenuation is a finished-material constraint.
For a homogeneous nonmagnetic medium n+i*kappa, a plane wave's intensity ratio over L is exp(-4*pi*kappa*L/lambda). A homogeneous1dB absorption budget over100um at650nm therefore requires kappa<=lambda*ln(10)/(40*pi*L)=1.1910203481790702e-4. This is a diagnostic, not a guided-mode theorem. Actual modes require dispersive modal energy, group velocity and material overlap; roughness, bends, finite confinement, couplers and structural disorder add losses. A final manufactured composite cannot inherit a lossless bulk refractive index merely from its constituents.

If N optical locations are critical and each has marginal bad-event probability at most p, then the probability of any bad event is at most N*p, with no independence assumption. N=500,p=2e-4 permits an upper bound0.1. This neither establishes those marginals nor says every structural defect is fatal. A correlated twin plane can make the relevant event and critical geometry entirely different. Conversely, error-tolerant photonic geometry may avoid demanding atomically perfect placement. Actual optical performance and the actual fabrication distribution must be connected.

The manufactured useful output includes both mode couplers. At a3dB end-to-end budget, independently allocating0.5dB to each port leaves2dB for propagation/bends/disorder. That is a design allocation, not a measured component. A low-loss isolated bend is not an end-to-end route.

Source bindings actually read:
Posnjak et al. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2310.10884v2, crystal-growth/conversion/optical passages pp3--10: DNA tetrapod diamond-lattice assembly, processing and optical experiments supply a material starting point; actual twinning, edge disorder and absorption remain. No prescribed3D defect-route device or manufacturing cost is supplied.
Yin et al. https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07877v1, torsional mechanisms/phase diagram/discussion: competing binding modes and magnesium/sequence-dependent phase selection; pure/mixed outcomes matter. A local desired contact does not certify a unique bulk phase or addressed route.
